requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`. I did not request implementation source, because the test's assertions settle each point.

- **Instructions on the first delivered result, even with no matches.** On `session`, `search_text` for "absent" returns an empty result. The test asserts that `instructions` is a string on it.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** On `session`, the earlier `search_text` call with the invalid pattern "(" is asserted to be an error. The next successful search is then the first to carry `instructions`.
- **Shared by text and structural searches.** `peer` is a separate session whose first search is a `search_structure` call with an empty result. It carries `instructions` equal to the text-search string, and its single outstanding search is that result.
- **Per conversation.** `fresh` and `peer` are new `SessionTools`. Each one's first successful result includes the same instructions. `hits["instructions"]` on `fresh` equals `instructions`.
- **Later searches omit the field.** After `peer` closes its first search, a later `search_text` result is asserted to have no `instructions` key. `session`'s later "hit" search also asserts `first.get("instructions").is_none()`.
- **Continuation pages omit the field.** The `get_next_page` results `rest` and `second` are each asserted to have no `instructions` key.
- **Content of the instructions.** The test checks that the instructions contain the phrases about closing every delivered page with `finish_search`, which tags to include, `used:[]` for none or an empty result, and not having read more source. This matches the cited `finish_search.mcp.description` guidance on when to call it and what to put in `used`.

Minor gaps, none of which I count against adequacy:
- A failed structural search is not exercised. The failed-search rule is stated for searches in general, and the failed text search establishes it.
- The `capped` second search on `fresh` has no explicit check that it omits `instructions`. That behaviour is checked on `peer` and `session`.

No gaps or acknowledgments apply.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
